documents.title: WFUMB guidelines on liver elastography update

chunks.content: WFUMB Guidelines and Policy document development strategy WFUMB Publications Committee 2026 OBJECTIVE The World Federation for Ultrasound in Medicine and Biology (WFUMB) and its affiliated Federations strive to intensify cooperation with joint guidelines and other policy documents in order to efficiently combine the potential and perspectives of its members, WFUMB aims to meet the highest scientific and methodological standards, ensuring evidence-based recommendations, and achieve worldwide clinical applicability and acceptance. This document updates the strategy for the creation and updating of joint Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPGs), position papers, and technical reviews [1,2] and describes principles, instruments, and logistics for coordinating these projects of WFUMB and its affiliated Federations. The process of development and updating of policy documents under the umbrella of WFUMB is based on a strategic plan and starts with decisions on topics, selection of experts and invitations of potential partners for collaboration. It includes shared principles on the review of evidence, the creation of recommendations and statements, grading of level of evidence and strength of recommendations, and the process to achieve consensus. Finally, rules for review, approval, endorsement, publication, and update of WFUMB policy documents are described. WFUMB GUIDELINE AND POLICY DOCUMENT PROJECTS CPGs of WFUMB and its affiliated federations shall provide ultrasound practitioners and physicians requesting ultrasound examinations and ultrasound-guided interventions with evidence-based recommendations derived from reliable scientific literature and resulting from a formal guideline developmental process. Position Statements describe WFUMB positions on important current issues in clinical applications, safety, education and training of ultrasound techniques or related health care policy issues. Technical Reviews give state-of-the art information on new ultrasound techniques and technologies for physicians, medical technologists, engineers and physicists applying or developing ultrasound technologies. WFUMB affiliated Federations are encouraged to initiate and develop their own guidelines and policy documents under the WFUMB umbrella, in collaboration with other member societies and, where appropriate, relevant external partners, to maximize and avoid overlapping or competing projects. GUIDELINE DEVELOPMENT GROUP A standing ‘Guideline Development Group’ is appointed to coordinate planning, development and updating of Clinical Practice guidelines, Position Papers and Technical Reviews of WFUMB and its affiliated Federations. The specific tasks are as follows: - Creation and annual updating of a register of the guidelines and other policy documents of the WFUMB and its affiliated Federations, including the date of publication, the steering group chair/ person responsible, and the reference to the published document. - Collection and evaluation of proposals for new guideline and policy document projects under the umbrella of WFUMB. - Preparation of a strategic 10-year plan for the revision and update of guidelines and policy documents, to be approved by the WFUMB Administrative Council (AC). - Review of selection of members of steering groups, working groups and Delphi panels according to the criteria outlined in the related paragraphs below including evaluation of potential conflicts of interest (COIs) - Maintain contact with all Guideline Steering Committees and those persons responsible for other policy documents to monitor the progress of projects, identify and prioritize needs for methodological, financial, and scientific support, and coordinate this support in accordance with decisions made by the WFUMB Publications Committee, Safety Committee and Executive Board (ExB) and, if necessary, other bodies such as the responsible committees and ExBs of affiliated Federations. The group shall consist of one representative of WFUMB ExB (who is chairing the group), one member each from the Publications Committee and the Safety Committee of WFUMB, a statistician and a person with expertise in librarian skills. All members should have extensive experience in guidelines methodology and development. NEW GUIDELINE AND POLICY DOCUMENT PROJECTS Suggestions for topics of new WFUMB guidelines and policy document projects (e.g., guidelines, position statements and technical reviews) can be made by the members of the WFUMB ExB, AC, publication committee, other standing WFUMB committees and the editorial board of the WFUMB journals (Ultrasound in Medicine and Biology, WFUMB Ultrasound Open) and the delegates/boards of the WFUMB affiliated Federations. Suggestions from other international medical societies wishing to cooperate with WFUMB to develop a joint guideline or other policy documents will also be considered. The proposal should include the rationale for a WFUMB (or joint) guideline/policy document on the topic in question, as well as a description of the overall objectives and clinical/technical questions to be addressed. It should also include information on the target users and suggestions for potential collaborations. The proposal is submitted to the ‘Guideline Development Group’ for review under the following criteria: - Clinical relevance of the topic - Significant difference to existing guidelines/ internationally acknowledged policy documents - Realistic possibility of implementing the project by WFUMB, including regular updates. The recommendation of the ‘Guideline Development Group’ is then submitted to the Publications Committee and, depending on its content, to the Safety Committee for comment and finally to the ExB for approval. The proposal is submitted to the ‘Guideline Development Group’ for review under the following criteria: - Clinical relevance of the topic - Significant difference to existing guidelines/ internationally acknowledged policy documents - Realistic possibility of implementing the project by WFUMB, including regular updates. The recommendation of the ‘Guideline Development Group’ is then submitted to the Publications Committee and, depending on its content, to the Safety Committee for comment and finally to the ExB for approval. STEERING COMMITTEE and EXPERT WORKING GROUP Guidelines and policy documents are developed by expert groups led by a steering committee. Each CPGs project is coordinated and managed by a steering committee, consisting of representatives of the affiliated Federations of WFUMB. The ‘Guidelines Development Group’ requests that each affiliated Federation appoints one representative to serve on the steering committee who is acknowledged by their outstanding contributions to the topic of the guidelines, in particular through innovative research, extensive practical experience related to the topic(s) of the guidelines (indicated also by high-quality original research articles listed in PubMed and Scopus) and by experience in guideline methodology. Depending on the scope of the project, a steering committee may not be necessary for position statements and technical reviews. In this case, a project leader and their deputy are appointed by the ‘Guideline Development Group’ and approved by the Publication Committee. The steering committee members and project leaders (including their deputies) must disclose any potential conflicts of interest (COI) by completing and signing a separate conflict of interest questionnaire, which is recorded and evaluated by the ‘Guideline Development Group’ and published as part of the guideline or other policy document. Significant COIs are relationships with companies or organizations related to guidelines through stock ownership, patents/royalties, or employment. Any significant COI is an exclusion criterion. For guidelines development, the steering committee elects its chairperson and a deputy at the first meeting (via conference call), discusses the outline of the document, identifying the different areas of CPGs topic, and sets the timeline. It is expected that the chairperson and the deputy will have extensive research and clinical experience on the topic as well as experience in guideline development and in chairing committees. The chairperson is responsible for coordinating the overall efforts of the steering committee, setting agendas, and ensuring that deadlines are met. The steering committee or project leaders are responsible for selecting the group of experts and, if necessary, decide to have a separate Delphi panel (see below). The ‘Guidelines Development Group’ receives bi-monthly updates on the development of CPGs or other policy documents and is acknowledged in the dedicated paragraph of the final document. The steering committee or project leaders decide on the type of experts needed for the specific topic of CPGs or other policy document project. It is crucial to ensure diversity within the expert group to provide a comprehensive perspective on the CPGs or policy document topic in terms of both scientific substance and global clinical application. Therefore, the steering committee or project leaders should also consider inviting other international scientific societies or special interest groups to recommend members to represent their specialist expertise (e.g. hepatology, pathology, OB/GYN/ statistics, etc.) if appropriate. Criteria to select working group members are based on transparent criteria as follows: -Outstanding contributions to the topic of the guidelines by innovative research work (indicated by high- quality research listed in PubMed and Scopus) and outstanding experience in clinical applications. - Fair representation of the affiliated Federations (with a minimum of one and a maximum of five experts per affiliated organization) and collaborating organizations. - Industry representatives are excluded. If a company is funding the guidelines, this should not entitle them to participate. Potential COI must be disclosed by all members of the working group and evaluated and recorded by the ‘Guideline Development Group’. Any significant COI (as outlined above) is an exclusion criterion. The selection of working group members is reviewed by the ‘Guideline Development Group’ and finally approved by the Publication Committee based on the selection criteria stated above. The different areas to be covered on the CPGs will be distributed between members of the steering group, so that each steering group member focuses on specific area(s) of the CPGs topic and is the chair of a subgroup for the development of CPGs in that area(s). The task of the subgroup chair is to facilitate discussions, gather input, and draft proposals for the assigned area(s). The chairs ensure that the subgroups stay focused on their objectives. The subgroups will regularly meet to discuss progress, share insights, and address any challenges they encounter, ensuring a comprehensive approach to their area(s) of the CPGs topic. For CPGs, each working group member is

distributed between members of the steering group, so that each steering group member focuses on specific area(s) of the CPGs topic and is the chair of a subgroup for the development of CPGs in that area(s). The task of the subgroup chair is to facilitate discussions, gather input, and draft proposals for the assigned area(s). The chairs ensure that the subgroups stay focused on their objectives. The subgroups will regularly meet to discuss progress, share insights, and address any challenges they encounter, ensuring a comprehensive approach to their area(s) of the CPGs topic. For CPGs, each working group member is encouraged to appoint a junior expert as a research specialist. Junior experts are up to 40 years old and have experience in research on the topic of CPGs. They have also published original articles as first author in peer-reviewed journals with an impact factor of at least 2.0 on the specific topic. To ensure transparency, their CV is distributed to all members of the steering committee and the working group. The junior experts or librarians will assist with the literature search and preparation of evidence tables. During the first meeting of the steering committee/ project leaders with the other working group members, consensus is reached regarding the structure of the document and distribution of tasks. A list of Delphi panel members is prepared. The Delphi panel comprises academic experts, expert users, other stakeholders and a patient representative, none of whom are part of the CPGs expert panel. The purpose of establishing a Delphi panel is to reduce bias and enable the working group members to reconsider their views based on the Delphi panel's collective responses whenever a recommendation has not a high level of evidence. The CPGs expert panel, i.e. the steering committee and the working group, and the ‘Guidelines Development Group’ jointly select the group to be consulted through the Delphi process, which takes place on an online platform where all CPGs documents are uploaded and reviewed. The selected Delphi panel members will receive an invitation to join the platform and will be asked to upload a disclosure form [3]. AUTHORSHIP and ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS The authors of CPGs or another policy document are the members of the steering committee/ project leaders and the other working group members (in alphabetical order). Corresponding and first/last authors are the steering committee’s chairperson or project leader and their deputies. Each author is expected to make substantial contributions to the design of the work, acquisition, analysis or interpretation of data. All authors must approve the submitted version and agree to be personally accountable for their own contribution. The ‘Guideline Development Group’ should not expect to be named as authors on papers. All junior experts are listed as authors. Members of the Delphi panel, librarians and others who provide advice or other kinds of support that do not qualify them as authors should be acknowledged. DEVELOPMENT PROCESS A systematic literature review is an essential element of all WFUMB CPGs and other policy documents. It is being carried out to ensure that the guidelines or the policy documents are based on the most current and comprehensive evidence available. This involves: - Defining the research questions and objectives (if comparing tests, according to the PICO format to specify Patient, Intervention, Comparison, and Outcome) based on agreement of the expert group members - Identifying and selecting relevant studies through a comprehensive search strategy, following a pre- defined protocol that specifies the databases (e.g., PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Google Scholar), inclusion and exclusion criteria, and the specific keywords and search strings to address the research questions. - The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 checklist will be applied (supplement 1) [4]. The results of the systematic literature search are synthesized using evidence tables, summarizing key findings, identifying patterns and inconsistencies, and determining the overall strength of the evidence based on the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine 2011 criteria (supplement 2) [5] and the QUADAS-2 tool for evaluating the accuracy of diagnostic studies (supplement 3) [6]. For CPGs and, if appropriate, also for position papers, the assessment of the methodological quality and scientific and clinical relevance of the selected studies and their key results is the basis for drafting evidence- based recommendations and/or statements in the subgroups. No formal recommendations are given in technical reviews. If substantial evidence to answer the research questions is lacking, recommendations and/or statements can be based on good clinical practice and expert opinion. The drafts for recommendations and/or statements shall also take into account resource implications, feasibility and accessibility, possible harms, and stakeholder implications. All recommendations and statements should be substantiated by a brief explanatory text that summarizes the underlying evidence and/or expert opinion in a comprehensible but concise manner. Once the sections are completed, they are discussed with the steering committee members,

If substantial evidence to answer the research questions is lacking, recommendations and/or statements can be based on good clinical practice and expert opinion. The drafts for recommendations and/or statements shall also take into account resource implications, feasibility and accessibility, possible harms, and stakeholder implications. All recommendations and statements should be substantiated by a brief explanatory text that summarizes the underlying evidence and/or expert opinion in a comprehensible but concise manner. Once the sections are completed, they are discussed with the steering committee members, who provide guidance and feedback to improve the quality of the drafts without overruling the other experts. The role of the steering committee is to gather and combine the results of the subgroups, ensuring there are no overlaps or inconsistencies. Finally, all recommendations and statements are presented to the whole panel of experts, and voted. An on- site consensus conference or electronic voting is used for this purpose. Recommendations and statements with >75% approval are adopted. Approved recommendations will be published in the final document together with the percentage of agreement (evidence-based and clinical practice recommendations) and the level of evidence according to the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine 2011 criteria [5] and the strength of recommendation as weak or strong according to Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) criteria (only evidence-based recommendations) [7]. Recommendations and statements with ≤ 75% approval and the comments from the Delphi process are reviewed by the steering committee. The steering committee will then make suggestions to the working group to develop alternatives or rephrase the respective recommendation, which will then be voted on again. If no consensus (>75% approval) can be reached in the following nominal group process, the results of the literature review and expert discussion will be integrated into the guideline without giving a formal recommendation. In the final document, the panel may formulate recommendations for further research, contributing to the research agenda. Once the document is finalized, the Delphi panel will be requested to indicate agreement or disagreement on all recommendations within a 10-day period. The Delphi panel’s feedback, presented as percentages, will be included in the supplementary material. Timeline A Gantt chart that illustrates the project schedule and timeline will be prepared by the steering committee at the first meeting. PUBLICATION Before submission, CPGs and other policy documents are submitted to the Publications Committee, Safety Committee and the WFUMB ExB for review and final approval. The review process and final approval only concern compliance with the basic rules and process steps published here, not with the content agreed upon by the panel of experts. Endorsement by other professional societies and international organizations may be requested. For WFUMB CPGs and other policy documents, publication in Ultrasound in Medicine and Biology (UMB) as open access or alternatively WFUMB Ultrasound Open is preferred, while CPGs and policy documents of a WFUMB affiliated Federation with participation of other Federations under the umbrella of WFUMB may preferentially be published in the official journals of the respective affiliated Federation. Joint publications in UMB and official journals of affiliated Federations or partner organizations may be sought in the interest of wide dissemination and acceptance. WFUMB papers undergo a peer review process according to the common rules and standards of the scientific journal. REVISION/ UPDATES Typically, CPGs are revised every five years unless they pertain to a rapidly changing field. In the latter case, a ‘living guideline process’ shall be initiated. Position papers and technical reviews are also reviewed after five years to determine whether they need to be updated or revised. The revision process and the commissioning of updates to CPGs and other policy documents are initiated by the ‘Guideline Development Group’. Preferably, the panel of experts responsible for the initial draft is commissioned again. If previous members are unavailable and/or additional personnel are required due to content-related requirements, the revision process is carried out in accordance with the principles outlined above. The ‘Guideline Development Group’ decides on the necessity of a selective update or, alternatively, a complete revision based on a proposal from the steering committee/project leader. References 1.
